digest.component_or_area: documentation — git workflow and ticket close process
propositions: Operator guidance was missing a critical step: after a change merges in Gerrit and before closing the ticket, contributors must fast-forward their own worktree (not the shared main checkout) to make the merged commit reachable from HEAD.

The close completion precheck (_referencing_commit_exists at transition_close.py:32-57) runs git log from repo_root with ref=HEAD to verify the rebar-ticket: commit is reachable; if the worktree is not advanced post-merge, the precheck fails with 'cannot confirm the work landed'.

Documentation in AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md must explicitly instruct: (a) run 'git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main' from inside your worktree after merge, (b) never fast-forward, reset, or stash the shared main checkout as it may contain uncommitted operator WIP.

AGENTS.md close-discipline section and new CONTRIBUTING.md §2f (After merge — fast-forward your worktree, THEN close the ticket) both carry the two-part guidance: worktree-only advance + shared checkout protection.
